input.question: If matter attracts matter (gravity), does anti-matter repel matter (anti-matter)?
input.ground_truth: Gravity is a response to mass, it doesn't care what kind of matter has the mass. Both matter and antimatter have mass, and so will attract each other. A normal hydrogen atom would be gravitationally attracted to an anti-hydrogen in exactly the same way that it would be attracted to a normal hydrogen. Dark Energy is unrelated to this concept -- it refers to the accelerated expansion of space itself in the universe.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: If matter attracts matter (gravity), does anti-matter repel matter (anti-matter)?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have magnets. Some magnets stick together because they are the same kind, and some magnets push away from each other because they are different kinds.

Now, think of matter (like everything you can touch) as one kind of magnet, and anti-matter as a different kind of magnet.

When matter meets matter, they pull together—like magnets that stick.

But when matter meets anti-matter, they push each other away—like magnets that repel!

So yes, anti-matter and matter push away from each other. That’s what “repel” means. 🧲🧲
